chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Isa ibn 'Umar, the client of the Ansar, that he asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man: is it lawful for him to shake hands with a Magian? He said:
No. Then he asked him: should he perform wudu (ablution) if he shakes hands with them? He said: Yes, indeed shaking hands with them invalidates wudu (ablution).

Shaykh Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The correct approach regarding this report is that we interpret it as referring to washing the hand, because that is also called wudu (ablution), as we have explained. That is only required because they are impure. We only said that because of the consensus of the sect that this does not necessitate the invalidation of wudu (ablution). Also, we have already presented the reports which contain that nothing invalidates wudu (ablution) except what exits from the two passages or sleep; and they are to be carried upon their generality, and it is not permissible to specify them on account of this anomalous report.

key_terms.إِجْمَاعِ الطَّائِفَةِ: the consensus of the Imamiyyah community
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), here discussed in its legal sense and also possibly as washing

ai.seo_question: Does shaking hands with a non-Muslim invalidate wudu (ablution) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on shaking hands with a Magian and the apparent implication for wudu (ablution). Shaykh Abu Ja'far clarifies that the report should be understood as requiring hand-washing due to impurity, not as actual invalidation of wudu (ablution), in light of the consensus of the Imamiyyah and other established hadith limiting nullifiers of wudu (ablution).
